approved: Migration Amendment (Limits on Immigration Detention) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change the Migration Act 1958 to better meet human rights standards on immigration detention.
It would cap most detention at 90 days, extendable only when the Minister judges the extension is a last resort, reasonable and proportionate under international law.
Detention of minors would be banned entirely.
Introduces a 90-day limit on immigration detention.
Allows the Minister to extend detention beyond 90 days under strict conditions.
Makes any detention extension reviewable by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
Non-citizens in Australia without a valid visa and minors who would otherwise be detained.
